title: EC2 instance families: matching the workload

kcs.statement: Each EC2 instance family suits a kind of workload: general purpose (M, T) for balanced web servers, compute optimized (C) for batch processing and gaming servers, memory optimized (R, X) for in-memory databases, storage optimized (I, D) for high local disk I/O, and accelerated computing (P, G) for GPU and machine learning work.

problem_ideas: Match five workloads (Redis-style in-memory cache, video transcoding farm, ML model training, low-traffic blog, data warehouse with heavy local scans) to an instance family.
A gaming company needs high single-thread CPU for game servers: which family, and why not memory optimized?
A distractor offers 'storage optimized' for a workload that stores all its data in S3: explain why it is wrong.
A real-time analytics engine keeps a 400 GB dataset in RAM: which family?
A company trains deep-learning models on GPUs: which family letter would you look for?
Spot the mismatch: 'Use compute optimized instances for a NoSQL database doing millions of random reads on local disks.'
